title: Length-aware selectivity for contains()/LIKE scan filters v2
summary: I added a TableFilterType::EXPRESSION_FILTER case to RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter in relation_statistics_helper.cpp. It applies when the filter is a positive match function (contains, ~~ (LIKE), like_escape, prefix or suffix) whose first argument is not foldable and whose second argument is a non-NULL VARCHAR constant. Let L be the literal length with %/_ excluded for LIKE, capped at 64. The selectivity is then max(0.2*0.75^L, 0.01) and the estimate is max(1, card*sel). Any other expression filter keeps the old behavior (the flat 0.2 default). The helper is a file-static function, so no header changed. The build is OK. Full bench: q09 went from 1227 to 763ms (-37.8%) and the geomean improved by 3.6%. Every other template was within noise. q04 showed +7.4% in the first run, but it has no LIKE, and a rerun gave -11.6%. A rerun of q09 gave 1200 to 770ms (-35.9%). Results checks passed in bench. I did not run `profile q09.m0`, so the join-order flip is inferred from the timing and not confirmed in a plan.
notes: This is the same mechanism as the earlier contains-selectivity run, and the q09 gain reproduced (-36..-38%). An earlier note said lineitem lost its bloom filter after the join-order flip; it still nets a large win. A possible follow-up is an ILIKE / regexp_matches literal-length estimate, but no visible query uses them.
